elements.content: Grammar focus: Distancing Passives & Reporting Structures.

Core Rule: Use impersonal passive constructions: It + Passive Reporting Verb + That-Clause ( It is claimed that... ) or Subject + Passive Reporting Verb + Perfect Infinitive ( The asset is reported to have appreciated... ).

Impersonal It-Passive — It + Passive Verb + that...: It is widely reported that legislative amendments will pass.
Subject + Infinitive Passive — Subject + Passive Verb + to have V3: The enterprise is understood to have acquired the subsidiary.
Adverbial Distancing — Allegedly / Reportedly + Clause: Reportedly , negotiations reached consensus late last night.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence correctly uses a subject reporting passive?
options: The firm is reported to have expanded into three new markets.
The firm is reported that expanded into three new markets.

elements.content: 2. What infinitive form reports an action completed prior to the reporting verb?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

The CEO is reported to have resigned.
It has been suggested that the plan failed.
He is understood to be abroad.
The data are alleged to have been altered.
